requirements.requirement: Create the opsbot account on node1 and the corresponding account/key material needed on node2.
requirements.summary: Direct observations show opsbot exists as UID 1000 on both nodes, with appropriately permissioned SSH material. The node1 public key and node2 authorized key have the same ED25519 fingerprint.

requirements.requirement: Allow opsbot on node1 to execute commands on node2 as opsbot using SSH keys.
requirements.summary: A key-authenticated SSH session from node1 directly executed commands on node2 as opsbot (UID 1000). The same behavior succeeded after both nodes restarted.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based SSH authentication for opsbot on both systems.
requirements.summary: Both nodes' effective user-specific SSH configuration requires publickey and disables password and keyboard-interactive authentication. Password-only attempts to both nodes were rejected with “Permission denied (publickey),” including after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed coherently for both nodes: each had a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity independently confirmed by lifecycle observations, and recovered SSH service, credentials/policy, verification data, and cross-node access.
limitations: Successful key authentication into node1 as opsbot was not demonstrated; however, the contract requires node1-to-node2 access and only requires that node1 enforce key-based authentication for opsbot. Effective configuration and negative password-only testing directly demonstrate that policy.
The captured password-attempt command text contains redaction artifacts, but its observed SSH responses and the independently inspected effective sshd configuration are coherent.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account/key creation, SSH policy changes and reloads, the remote verification marker, and sequential restarts all had clear roles in implementing the contract or completing the mandatory restart protocol. No failed services, damaged package state, new listening exposure, or abandoned temporary residue was observed after execution.
